macro.note: NYSE closed and a full bond-market close per SIFMA's recommended schedule. The BLS is closed. Canada also observes Labour Day. The knock-on matters for next week's calendar: the holiday pushes several standard release slots out by a day, including consumer credit and the EIA petroleum report.
Confirmed on Finance Canada's own published list: roughly C$27.6bn of US goods at rates of 15, 25 and 50 percent, in force from 12:01 AM on September 8.

Confirmed on the Federal Reserve's own September calendar. Labor Day pushes the fifth business day to Tuesday. The Treasury also auctions a 3-year note of $58bn this day; the auction TIME is unverified because the offering announcement does not publish until September 8, so it is not stated here.

macro.event: ECB Governing Council Day 1, Berlin; Census QSS
macro.note: The Governing Council convenes in Berlin, hosted by the Bundesbank, ahead of the September 10 decision. BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation and the Census Quarterly Services Survey both land at 10:00 AM ET. Treasury reopens the 10-year note at $39bn. CORRECTION carried from prior runs: the Bank of Canada does NOT announce this day - its September fixed date was the 2nd, where it held at 2.25%, and September 16 carries only the Summary of Deliberations at 1:30 PM ET.

Poll expects +25bp to 2.50%. Decision 8:15 AM ET, press conference 8:45 AM ET, in Berlin. IMPORTANT FRAMING CORRECTION: the move to 2.50% is a Reuters-poll EXPECTATION, not an ECB fact. The ECB's current key rates are deposit 2.25%, main refinancing 2.40% and marginal lending 2.65%, effective 17 June 2026, and the 23 July 2026 decision HELD. Brief the direction as a HIKE if it comes - framing the ECB as easing is wrong by direction - but do not state the hike as scheduled fact.

No verified poll median. First of the two inflation prints before the FOMC. A Continuum Economics forecast of +0.4% headline and +0.3% core was located but that is a single house view, NOT a poll median, and is labelled as such rather than presented as consensus. Wholesale trade 10:00 AM, natural gas storage 10:30 AM, and the EIA petroleum status report shifted to 12:00 PM by the Labor Day holiday. Treasury reopens the 30-year bond at $22bn. Oracle AND Adobe both report after the close.

macro.event: CPI, August - THE print the Fed named
macro.note: Reuters poll +0.4% headline / +0.2% core. The single most consequential scheduled release of the month, and the last major inflation reading before the FOMC decides. Governor Waller said on September 3 that his policy decision 'will be heavily influenced by what we learn about August inflation' - this is that reading, and it arrives with the Fed in communications blackout, so there will be no official reaction. Bloomberg Economics expects headline CPI to ACCELERATE to 3.4% year-over-year with core easing to 2.4%. Real Earnings also 8:30 AM, University of Michigan preliminary sentiment 10:00 AM, Business Formation Statistics 10:00 AM, and the Federal Reserve's Z.1 Financial Accounts at 12:00 PM.

Prices 42.6% hold / 57.4% hike on the 9/4 cohort. Decision at 2:00 PM ET with the press conference at 2:30 PM ET, both times confirmed on the Federal Reserve's own September 2026 calendar page - this closes a previously unverified item. The September 4 FedWatch cohort prices 42.6% hold against 57.4% for a 25 basis point hike; other estimates span 51% to 65%, so brief it as a range. Probability of a CUT is exactly zero. The Bank of Japan meets September 17-18 and is widely expected to hike; its statement time is unverified. The Fed communications blackout runs from today, September 5, through September 17.

earnings.note: Oracle reports after the close on September 10, confirmed from company investor relations. The most consequential single earnings report of next week as a read on AI infrastructure demand and backlog conversion - and it now lands the day before CPI, into a market that has just repriced the policy path higher.

Adobe reports after the close on September 10, confirmed from company investor relations. Read as a check on whether software that monetises AI usage is still being rewarded - the dividing line that separated the winners from the losers across the whole of last week's earnings cohort.
